Original Requirements: Build the Volopa OOP (Out-of-Pocket) Expenses API System using Laravel 10+ with PHP 8.2+. Three modules: 1. User Management & Permissions — RBAC via user_feature_permission with delegation hierarchy 2. Pocket Expense CSV Batch Upload — synchronous validation, async background sync 3. Single Expense Data Capturing — CRUD with FX conversion and flexible metadata
Product Goals: Enable employees to record out-of-pocket expenses incurred outside the Volopa card system
Provide a delegatable permission hierarchy so admins can manage expenses on behalf of users
Support both single-entry and CSV batch upload for expense data capturing
Deliver automated FX conversion so multi-currency expenses are normalized to client wallet base currency
Ensure data integrity through atomic validation and transaction handling
Maintain security through OAuth2 authentication and role-based access control
Provide comprehensive audit trail for permission grants/revokes and expense operations
Support operational efficiency through bulk historical expense entry via CSV
Enable flexible expense categorization through configurable metadata and sources
Deliver consistent API responses following Laravel best practices and Volopa standards
User Stories: As a Primary Administrator, I want to have full access to all users' expenses by default so I can manage the entire organization's out-of-pocket expenses
As an Administrator, I want to manage my own expenses and receive delegation rights for specific users so I can help with expense management without full access
As a Business User, I want to create, view, edit and delete my own out-of-pocket expenses so I can track my business expenses
As a Card User, I want to record expenses I paid with cash or personal cards so they're tracked alongside my Volopa card transactions
As an Admin with management rights, I want to create, edit, and approve expenses for my delegated users so I can assist with their expense management
As a Primary Admin, I want to grant and revoke management rights to other users so I can distribute expense management workload
As a user, I want to upload a CSV file with up to 200 expense records so I can efficiently enter bulk historical expenses
As a user, I want detailed validation errors with line numbers when my CSV upload fails so I can quickly fix the issues
As a user, I want automatic FX conversion when I enter expenses in different currencies so I don't have to calculate exchange rates manually
As a user, I want to override the automatic FX conversion if needed so I can use specific rates when required
As a client, I want configurable expense sources (Cash, Corporate Card, Personal Card, Other) so I can categorize expenses by payment method
As a user, I want to attach metadata like categories, tracking codes, and projects to expenses so they integrate with existing Volopa classification systems
As a user, I want to receive notifications when my batch CSV upload is completed so I know the processing status
As an admin, I want to select which user the CSV expenses should be created for so I can bulk-create expenses on behalf of team members
As a system, I want all-or-nothing validation for CSV uploads so partial uploads don't create data inconsistencies
Competitive Analysis: Expensify: Strong mobile app and receipt OCR, but limited delegation hierarchy and no CSV batch upload for admin-managed users
Concur SAP: Enterprise-grade approval workflows and integrations, but complex setup and expensive for mid-market
Zoho Expense: Good integration with Zoho suite and multi-currency support, but limited role-based delegation features
Rydoo: Strong European market presence with good mobile UX, but lacks fine-grained permission delegation
Chrome River: Robust approval workflows and audit trails, but poor user experience and limited bulk import options
Receipt Bank (now Dext): Excellent document capture and categorization, but weak in delegation and multi-user expense management
Volopa Card System: Existing card transaction tracking with strong security and client isolation, but missing out-of-pocket expense capture

Requirement Analysis: The Volopa OOP Expenses system addresses a critical gap in expense management by capturing out-of-pocket expenses that occur outside the existing card transaction system. The system must integrate seamlessly with existing Volopa infrastructure including OAuth2 authentication, multi-tenant client isolation, and existing master data (currencies, categories, tracking codes). Key technical challenges include: (1) Complex permission delegation system that goes beyond standard RBAC to support dynamic user-to-user management assignments, (2) Atomic CSV validation and processing that ensures data integrity while providing detailed error feedback, (3) Real-time FX conversion with fallback mechanisms and user override capabilities, (4) Flexible metadata system that integrates with existing Volopa classification structures. The solution must maintain Volopa's security standards while providing operational efficiency through bulk import capabilities and delegation features that reduce administrative bottlenecks.
Requirement Pool: Implement OAuth2 authentication middleware and role-based permission system with user_feature_permission table supporting delegation hierarchy
Create pocket_expense core data model with FX conversion, status workflow (draft/submitted/approved/rejected), and soft delete capabilities
Develop CSV batch upload with synchronous validation (max 200 rows), atomic creation, and detailed error reporting with line-by-line feedback
Implement single expense CRUD operations with automatic FX conversion using /wallet-ccy-value endpoint and 30-day rate lookback
Build configurable expense source management (Cash, Corporate Card, Personal Card, Other) with client-specific customization up to 20 sources
Create flexible metadata system linking expenses to existing categories, tracking codes, projects, and additional fields via pocket_expense_metadata
Implement notification system for batch upload completion and audit logging for permission grant/revoke operations
UI Design draft: The system is primarily an API backend with minimal UI requirements. Key API interface elements include: (1) RESTful endpoints under /api/v1 with consistent JSON response formatting, (2) Form request validation classes with detailed error messages and field-level validation rules, (3) API Resources for consistent data serialization hiding internal fields, (4) CSV upload endpoint with file validation and error response formatting, (5) Permission management endpoints integrated with existing Settings > Manage Users UI path, (6) FX conversion API returning both original and converted amounts with rate information, (7) Expense source configuration endpoints returning dropdown-ready data structures. All responses follow Laravel API conventions with proper HTTP status codes (200, 201, 400, 401, 403, 404, 422) and consistent error formatting.

These decisions may require input from platform architecture team or existing codebase review.
